land.text: central Dalmatia, which the Delmatae took out of the rule of Gentius

predecessors.note: illyrian-kingdom's ledger has the Dalmatae and Daorsi declare independence in 180 on the Gentius page; the Dalmatae page says 181.

land.text: Dalmatia, where the Roman-Dalmatae Wars 'lasted until 33 BC when Octavian' installed Roman hegemony

successors.note: roman-republic ends 32 in Cliopatria; the Dalmatian coast north of Lissus is Octavian's conquest of 35-33 on its dossier.

capitals.name: Delminium (near Tomislavgrad)
capitals.note: 'Their capital settlement Delminium was located close to present-day Tomislavgrad' (Dalmatae page); Patsch located it 9 km south-east of Tomislavgrad at the Lib mountain (Delminium page). Coordinates are the researcher's reading of that. Destroyed in the first Dalmatian war, 156-155; the pages name no later capital. [Reviewer eu-02-x, 2026-10-19: 'to' -156 to -155: 'The first Dalmatian war in 156-155 BC finished with the destruction of capital Delminium' (Dalmatae page)]

correction.text: the Delmatae's territory (Delminium page): 'The coast and hinterland of central Dalmatia up to and beyond the Dinaric mountains', divided by Strabo into an inland and a coastal part separated by the Dinaric Alps

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Dalmatae, and its Roman Republic shape covers 41 of the Dalmatia region's 48 cells in every year sampled from 150 to 40 BC (none in 175; checked with the gazetteer on 2026-10-19), so the shape contradicts these independent Delmatae until 33 BC; roman-republic's ledger keeps the Dalmatian coast north of Lissus outside until Octavian (35-33) but none of its keyframes subtracts Dalmatia. The gazetteer's Dalmatia region is 12,100 km2 with bbox 15.2-18.4 E, 42.5-44.9 N and takes in Delminium at its inland edge; the pages give no area and no frontier. The Daorsi of the Neretva valley and the Greek colonies of the coast (Issa, Pharos) are inside the box but are not the Delmatae's; illyrian-kingdom's 180 loss uses the same region for both peoples.

correction.text: Dalmatia without Salona, which the Romans captured in 76 BC at the end of the third Dalmatian war

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The third Dalmatian war 78-76 BC finished with the capture of Salona.' The 15 km disc stands for the city and its coast; the page does not say whether the Romans kept it.

ledger.note: 181: the Delmatae throw off Gentius. They rejected the rule of Gentius, Pleuratus III's son (paraphrased), and 'appear in historical record for the first time in 181 BC'; the illyrian-kingdom dossier, from the Gentius page, dates the declaration of independence to 180. The land is the researcher's reading of the Delminium page's 'The coast and hinterland of central Dalmatia'.

156: the first Dalmatian war. 'The first Dalmatian war in 156-155 BC finished with the destruction of capital Delminium by consul Scipio Nasica'; the Delminium page: 'In 156 BC, the first conflict between the Dalmatae and the Romans took place' and the Dalmatae 'attacked Roman guard posts near the Neretva'.

155: Delminium destroyed. The war ended 'with the destruction of capital Delminium by consul Scipio Nasica' (the Delminium page puts the defeat in the year after the first conflict). The Delmatae keep their land.

region.text: Salona and the central Dalmatian coast

ledger.note: 78: the third Dalmatian war. 'The third Dalmatian war 78-76 BC finished with the capture of Salona.' (The second war, 119-118, moved no border on the page.)

region.text: Salona and the central Dalmatian coast

ledger.note: 76: Salona captured. 'The third Dalmatian war 78-76 BC finished with the capture of Salona.'
76: Salona passes to Rome. The third war 'finished with the capture of Salona'; the Delminium page names 'Salona (Solin)' as the Adriatic end of the roads to the Balkan interior.
34: Octavian's Illyricum expedition. 'The fourth and final conflict occurred 34-33 BC during Octavian's expedition to Illyricum.'

33: the Roman-Dalmatae Wars end. They 'lasted until 33 BC when Octavian' installed Roman hegemony; the last revolts under their federal leader Bato fall in 12 BC and the Great Illyrian Revolt in AD 6-9, after the end drawn here.

33: Octavian ends Dalmatian independence. The Roman-Dalmatae Wars 'lasted until 33 BC when Octavian' installed Roman hegemony; 'their resistance was finally quelled in the Great Illyrian revolt that ended in 9 AD' (Delminium page).

wars.name: First Dalmatian war
wars.outcome: Rome won; the consul Scipio Nasica destroyed Delminium, the capital.
wars.note: The Delminium page says only 'In 156 BC, the first conflict between the Dalmatae and the Romans took place'.

wars.name: Second Dalmatian war
wars.outcome: The page gives the dates only: 'The second Dalmatian war was fought in 119-118 BC'; no border moved on the pages opened.

wars.name: Third Dalmatian war
wars.outcome: Rome captured Salona and the war ended.

wars.name: Fourth Dalmatian war
wars.outcome: Octavian's expedition to Illyricum ended the Roman-Dalmatae Wars in 33 BC and installed Roman hegemony.
wars.note: During the Roman civil war of 49-44 BC the Delmatae supported Pompey (page); no land moved.

certainty.note: The pages name a capital and rivers' neighbourhood (the Neretva) but no frontier; the Dalmatia region is a stand-in for the 'coast and hinterland of central Dalmatia'.

sources.title: Dalmatae
sources.note: First mention and secession from Gentius 181; capital Delminium; territory; the four Dalmatian wars 156-155, 119-118, 78-76, 34-33; Bato 12 BC; the revolt AD 6-9.

sources.title: Delminium
sources.note: Capital's location near Tomislavgrad; first conflict with Rome 156; 'Dalmataes attacked Roman guard posts near the Neretva'; Salona as the coastal roads' end.

notes: Two pages. A tribal federation (the page speaks of a 'federal leader Bato' in 12 BC) whose territory no page measures; the Dalmatia region is a stand-in, so the keyframes are soft and their edges (the Neretva valley of the Daorsi, the coastal Greek colonies, the inland limit past the Dinaric mountains) are unknown. End 33 follows the page's 'Roman-Dalmatae Wars lasted until 33 BC'; the later revolts (12 BC, AD 6-9) are not drawn as a state. Pages differ by a year on the secession (181 here, 180 on the Gentius page that illyrian-kingdom cites) and the Delminium page does not date the destruction (the Dalmatae page: 156-155). The second war (119-118) is dated but has no territorial result on the pages. Not on any page: the territory in any year, the Daorsi and their relation to the Delmatae, the Roman protectorate of 167-148 over the southern Illyrian lands (roman-republic's dossier keeps the Dalmatian coast north of Lissus outside until Octavian), the Delmatae's own capital after 155. Delminium's coordinates are the researcher's reading of 'close to present-day Tomislavgrad' and 'Lib mountain'.
